content:
alex: Heads-up — saw weird evictions on prod last night. Pages that were referenced ~10s before a request were already evicted. Suspect page metadata staleness from the async reconciler :eyes:

marta: Which workload / model? any logs?

alex: quick snip from the evictor logs:```
[23:41:12] page=0x7fabc ref_ts=2329998815 last_access_ms=2329998815 resident=false evict=1
[23:41:13] req model=gptx sequence=64 hit_kv=false touch_page=0x7fabc --> miss
```
It looks like last_access got overwritten or never updated across the reconciler boundary.

ravi: That smells like a race between the residency updater (async) and the evictor/compactor. We update residency in a background thread that batches VMA updates. If the batch lags, the evictor sees stale resident=false.

sam: Two options: (A) make the residency update synchronous on touch (expensive), (B) attach a per-VMA generation counter to page meta so reconciler bumps gen and evictor compares. Gen avoids moving timestamps but does add per-touch CAS.

marta: Could also try a cheaper heuristic: write a small "stale" bit into page meta when reconciler schedules the VMA update; evictor skips pages with STALE for a short window. No heavy counters.

ravi: Skip sounds tempting but watch out for starvation under steady fragmentation. If evictor keeps skipping, compaction can't progress. Maybe bounded-skip: skip for X ms, after which we re-evaluate even if STALE.

sam: Another middle ground: maintain monotonic last_access that reconciler can only increase (atomic max). Evictor reads last_access; if delta < threshold treat as fresh. Avoids per-VMA gen but requires atomic max on write.

alex: Key constraint: offload/backpressure systems (KV cache, host staging) consume that metadata. If the metadata is inconsistent we over-evict and cause QPS fallbacks. So whatever solution must surface consistent signals to routing layer.

marta: Prototype plan I propose: add STALE bit + skip window = 50ms. Emit metrics: stale_pages_ratio, avg_stale_hold_ms, evict_after_stale_ms. Also expose a force-bypass metric when memory_pressure > 0.8. I'll spike this in allocator branch. :+1:

ravi: I'll implement the safety path: on memory_pressure > 85% we bypass STALE and allow eviction. Also add a small jitter to avoid thundering herd.

sam: I'll own the metric dashboards and a small load test harness to replay the high-frag workload (random small-alloc churn) so we can tune skip window.

alex: Action items: 1) marta spike STALE + metrics (ETA EOW) 2) ravi safety bypass + jitter 3) sam load harness + dashboard 4) run canary and collect stale_pages_ratio and fallback QPS delta.

marta: I'll push a WIP PR, will annotate with microbench numbers.

offload-bot: canary-deploy: started canary for alloc-spike-staleflag on staging (deploy id: can-2026-03-20-17)

alex: Great — please post results in this thread when available. Thanks all. :rocket:
